title: Vinted Is Asking Me to Post Back a Counterfeit Item — Do I Have To?
intro: If Vinted has confirmed the item is counterfeit, no — you don't have to return it. Its refund policy says it outright: "Items that are confirmed counterfeit don't need to be returned to receive a refund." The trap is the word "confirmed". When Vinted says there isn't strong evidence, buyers get pushed down the ordinary return path — and by default, they pay the postage. Here's how to get the refund either way.
meta_description: Vinted told you to post a counterfeit item back? Vinted's own policy says confirmed counterfeits don't need returning — here's how to get refunded without posting a fake.
author: Supervint Team
cta_text: Never miss a mispriced listing again — get instant alerts for the items you want on Vinted

body.heading: Why Vinted is asking you to post a fake back to the seller
paragraphs: The same sequence appears over and over on r/vinted, r/vintedUK and r/VintedAdvice. A buyer receives something they immediately recognise as counterfeit — wrong materials, wrong stitching, a serial number that doesn't match. They open a dispute with photos. Vinted's reply either calls the item authentic, or says there isn't enough evidence about its authenticity, and then offers a single route to a refund: send it back, at your own cost.

One of the most recent threads is typical. A buyer who had the item checked against authentic versions in a retail store was still told to post it back for a refund, and kept getting what they described as templated replies that refused to escalate the case. Months earlier, other buyers reported the same outcome — the refund withheld until the fake goes back, with the return postage landing on them.

What stings is the logic of it. You paid a Buyer Protection fee, the seller broke Vinted's own rules by listing a counterfeit, and you're now asked to pay to post the evidence back to them. Vinted's standard answer is that the default sits in the T&Cs you accepted — the same T&Cs that say no counterfeit item may be sold on the platform at all.

body.heading: What Vinted's own policy actually says
paragraphs: Vinted's policy is on your side here, and it's worth knowing the exact wording before you reply. Its help page "Item seems to be counterfeit" (help article 1471) states it plainly: if there's strong evidence the item is counterfeit, Vinted cancels the order and refunds you — and you won't have to return the item.
The refund policy (help article 465) repeats it in the section on items significantly not as described: items that are confirmed counterfeit don't need to be returned to receive a refund.

So the rule that makes you post a fake back is not Vinted's rule about counterfeits at all — it's the general return rule. When an item is handled as a normal "not as described" case, the refund policy says you may be asked to return it, and buyers pay return shipping as part of the Terms and Conditions unless the seller chooses to cover it with a Vinted-generated label. The counterfeit exception only applies once Vinted agrees that's what the item is.

body.heading: The word "confirmed" is where this goes wrong
paragraphs: Everything hinges on Vinted agreeing. Its counterfeit page asks for photos of the whole item, the suspicious parts of it, the care label on all pages and sides, and the serial number — high quality, in natural light, text readable. If Vinted sees no strong evidence of counterfeiting, it treats the item as authentic, completes the order, releases your payment to the seller, and you can no longer return it through Vinted at all.

That's the gap. Buyers who had the piece checked in a shop, or compared it to items they own, still report being told there isn't enough information about authenticity — and are then routed down the ordinary return path. In one widely-read thread the buyer summed it up: Vinted wouldn't confirm the authenticity, so the only solution offered was to send it back, at their own expense.

The practical lesson: stop arguing about the seller's behaviour and give Vinted exactly what its own page asks for. Make the claim specifically that the item is counterfeit — not faulty, not the wrong fit, not a change of mind. Those wordings drop you straight into the standard return flow, where you pay the postage.

body.heading: Do I have to post a counterfeit item back?
paragraphs: This is the part buyers agonise over, and the threads are full of the same warning: it is not something to do casually. Trading in counterfeit goods is a criminal offence in the UK under the Trade Marks Act 1994, and posting the piece back puts an item you now know to be fake into the postal system, returning it to a seller who — in the cases buyers describe — relists it. Commenters on r/VintedAdvice put it bluntly: it is completely illegal for you to post a counterfeit item. Treat that as the community's position rather than a line from Vinted's policy, and as a strong reason to push for the no-return refund.
You do have a genuine choice, and buyers use both options:

Push for the no-return refund. Supply authentication evidence — a third-party authentication service, written confirmation from a brand or retailer who checked it, or detailed side-by-side comparison photos — and say clearly you are reporting the item as counterfeit, not requesting a normal return. Buyers report this working: one described messaging Vinted that they shouldn't pay return postage on a fake, sending photos of how a genuine item should look, answering a couple of follow-up questions, then being refunded with no return required. Others report a full refund and keeping the item.

Return it, if that is the only way you get paid. If Vinted won't confirm the counterfeit and you still want the money, the return is the route — but do it defensively. The seller can cover postage by providing a Vinted return label, and in at least one r/vintedUK case they did exactly that once it was clear the listing was the problem.

body.heading: If you do send it back, protect yourself at every step
paragraphs: The risk buyers worry about — and it isn't paranoid — is the seller claiming the parcel came back holding something different from what was sent. Vinted's return conditions require the item to arrive in the condition reported, with all accessories, tags and labels. If they aren't met, your refund request can be disputed. Photographs and video are your defence.

Experienced commenters give the same checklist every time: photograph the item as it arrived, film it being repacked, photograph the sealed parcel, and photograph it going into the locker or over the counter. Use only the Vinted-generated return label — never arrange a private return through chat. Keep the original packaging until the case is closed. And mind the clocks: you have 2 calendar days from Vinted notifying you the order should have arrived to press "I have an issue", and 5 business days to send the return once the seller requests it. Miss either window and your payment can be released to the seller.

If the fake reappears on the seller's profile after the return, report the listing. Buyers describe doing exactly that — and it's often the only thing that happens to the seller. Vinted's counterfeit help page says it will take action against sellers who repeatedly sell counterfeit items, and its counterfeit policy (help article 307) says listings offering counterfeit items are permanently removed and the account suspended.

body.heading: How to get past the templated replies
paragraphs: The single most repeated complaint in these threads is that support sends back the same three or four sentences whatever you write — that the decision stands, that there's nothing more they can do. There is a way through it.

Open the Help Centre in the app (Profile → Help Center) or go to vinted.com/help, open any help article related to your issue and scroll to the very bottom. A "Contact us" / "I still need help" button appears there and opens the support form without needing an order attached. On the web, vinted.com/help/615 is the official "Contact us" page, with the contact option at the end of it.

When you write, keep it to facts and policy: the item is counterfeit, here is the evidence help article 1471 asks for, and here is the line from your refund policy saying confirmed counterfeits don't need to be returned. Ask explicitly for the case to be escalated to a human. If the issue is legal or regulatory and the normal form can't resolve it, Vinted's contacts for dispute resolution page (help article 1253) lists legal@vinted.com. As a last resort, note that Vinted's own dispute-resolution page asks you to contact Vinted first and warns that opening a payment dispute with your bank can lead to your account being restricted — buyers report chargebacks working, but it carries the most risk to your account.

body.heading: How to avoid buying a fake in the first place
paragraphs: Once the parcel is open, the burden falls on you, so the cheapest defence is at the listing stage. Ask for extra photos before you commit — the serial number, the care label, hardware and stitching close-ups, original packaging — and treat a refusal as information. Be cautious of prices far below the going rate, especially on the brands that are counterfeited relentlessly, and read the seller's feedback for other buyers mentioning fakes. And don't take your time: with Buyer Protection you have just 2 calendar days after delivery to raise an issue.

faq.question: Am I legally required to return a counterfeit item I bought on Vinted?
faq.answer: Vinted's policy doesn't require it once it confirms the item is counterfeit — help article 1471 says you won't have to return it, and the refund policy says confirmed counterfeits don't need to be returned to get a refund. Because trading in counterfeit goods is a criminal offence in the UK (Trade Marks Act 1994), buyers on r/vinted and r/VintedAdvice warn against posting fakes at all. Push for the no-return refund first.

faq.question: Vinted says it can't confirm the item is counterfeit — what happens then?
faq.answer: If Vinted sees no strong evidence of counterfeiting, it treats the item as authentic, completes the order and releases your payment — after which you can't return it through Vinted. So supply photos in the exact format help article 1471 lists (whole item, suspicious parts, care label on all pages and sides, serial number, in natural light) and ask for the case to be escalated. If it still isn't confirmed, you'll be pushed into an ordinary return.

faq.question: Do I have to pay return postage to send back a fake?
faq.answer: If the case is handled as an ordinary not-as-described return, yes by default: the refund policy says buyers pay return shipping as part of the Terms and Conditions, unless the seller chooses to provide a Vinted return label. The way to avoid it entirely is a confirmed-counterfeit refund, which Vinted's policy says requires no return at all.

faq.question: How long do I have to report a counterfeit on Vinted?
faq.answer: You have 2 calendar days from the moment Vinted notifies you the order should have arrived to press "I have an issue". If the seller then requests a return, you have 5 business days to send it, and the seller has 2 days to confirm the returned item is OK. Miss a window and the case can close with your payment released to the seller.

faq.question: Can Vinted make me send the fake back and then refuse my refund?
faq.answer: Vinted's return conditions require the item to come back in the condition reported, with all accessories, tags and labels. If that isn't met, your refund request can be disputed — which is why buyers film the repacking, photograph the sealed parcel, and use only the Vinted-generated return label.

faq.question: What if the seller relists the counterfeit after I return it?
faq.answer: Report the listing. Vinted's counterfeit policy (help article 307) says listings offering counterfeit items are permanently removed and the account suspended, and the counterfeit help page says Vinted will take action against sellers who repeatedly sell counterfeits. Buyers in the threads describe reporting the relisting and having it taken down.
